reviewerDerivedProposition: A 420 mL bladder with urgency in a frail postoperative client who just became lightheaded on standing is the need that can cause immediate harm, through either an unassisted attempt to get up or incontinence-driven moisture on already compromised sacral skin. The nurse facilitates safe voiding now - raised bedside commode, analgesia given as preparation for the transfer rather than as an end in itself, fall precautions with two-person assist, and orthostatic monitoring - rather than replacing the catheter that was removed six hours ago, waiting for pain to reach zero, or confining her to bed in a brief.
requiredFacts: Foley removed at 0600, no void since, urgency and lower abdominal pressure, bladder scan 420 mL - stage_2.
The failed standing attempt and the orthostatic drop from 126/70 to 104/62 with a rise to 96 - stage_2.
Pain 5/10 with last hydromorphone at 0300, establishing that analgesia is available - stage_2.
The coccygeal non-blanchable erythema and moisture risk that make incontinence consequential - baseline and stage_2.
disclosureEvidence: stage_2 presents the competing demands without ranking them or naming an approach. Hiding stage_3 is NECESSARY: stage_3 records that she 'transferred to a raised bedside commode with armrests using two-person assist' and 'voided twice on the commode', which is keyed option q3_a demonstrated as successful. The current fail-open render therefore discloses this item and the anchor genuinely repairs it.
clinicalVerdict: Correct. The keyed priority correctly treats analgesia as preparation for a safe transfer rather than as a competing goal, which is the subtlety that makes distractor q3_c wrong. Distractor q3_b is properly wrong on catheter-associated infection grounds: sensation and urgency are intact and returning bladder function should be facilitated before reinstrumentation, and the rationale correctly keeps the retention algorithm available if she cannot void, so the option is defeated without teaching that catheterisation is never appropriate at this volume. Distractor q3_e is properly wrong because bedrest with an absorbent brief increases moisture exposure over already compromised sacral skin, and q3_d correctly ranks nutrition below an immediate fall and moisture risk. I found no invented fact, no stranded value, no key ambiguity and no all-correct degeneracy.
bilingualVerdict: PARALLEL - I read the Chinese against the English for the stem, all five options and all five byChoice rationales. Each pair is semantically equivalent, including the compound keyed option. No language-specific defect.
sourcesChecked: No external premise was load-bearing for the prioritisation, which rests on chart findings I verified individually against the stage_2 exhibit. The catheter-avoidance principle underlying distractor q3_b is standard CAUTI-prevention practice and the item's rationale states it without overreaching.
siblingImpact: NONE. This is an anchor-only repair; no learner-facing text changes.
repairConstraints: Set answerableAfterStageId to stage_2. No content change is required or authorised by this row.
Do not anchor at baseline: the bladder volume, the urgency and the orthostatic episode all occur in stage_2.
If the sibling q4 repair edits stage_2, this row must be re-checked, though the q4 repair as scoped touches only option text.
criticalNote: This row survives affirmative scrutiny as a true anchor-only repair, and the anchor does real work by hiding a stage that demonstrates the keyed approach succeeding.
agreementReasoning: I derived stage_2 independently and independently identified stage_3's successful commode voids as the disclosure the anchor must hide. Codex reached the same boundary with no content work. I tested rather than accepted the no-defect claim, checking in particular whether the catheter distractor was defeated by an overreaching absolute rule - it is not - and whether any option depended on an unestablished fact, which is the defect that converts the sibling q4 row. The Campaign-16 producer's stage_2 was correct and the checker's baseline was too early.

reviewerDerivedProposition: The plan must answer each active driver without solving one at another's expense: optimise analgesia before activity so pain stops limiting mobility, apply orthostatic and fall precautions that answer the failed standing attempt, support intake in a client with weight loss and low albumin, maintain the pressure and moisture regimen including verified heel suspension, and institute prompted voiding so urgency never again forces an unsafe transfer. Keeping the head of bed above forty-five degrees whenever supine would worsen sacral shear over skin that is already compromised.
requiredFacts: The failed standing attempt and orthostatic values - stage_2.
Poor intake, the 7 lb loss, albumin 2.8 and prealbumin 14 - baseline.
The coccygeal Stage 1 area, the pressure regimen and heel suspension in place - baseline and stage_1.
The urgency-driven unsafe transfer risk - stage_2.

UNESTABLISHED FACTS ASSERTED BY KEYED OPTION q4_a: 'ordered ice' and 'hearing aids'. I searched the parent. The order set in baseline_record lists hip precautions, physical therapy evaluation, incentive spirometry, sequential compression devices, enoxaparin, clear liquids and Foley removal - there is no ice order. Nothing anywhere establishes hearing impairment or hearing aids; the baseline documents mild cognitive impairment, which is a different thing.
disclosureEvidence: stage_2 supplies the drivers but no plan. Hiding stage_3 is substantive: stage_3 shows the successful transfers and introduces the new device-related heel injury, which would both confirm the keyed mobility interventions and pre-empt the sibling q5 row.
clinicalVerdict: Five of the six options are correctly keyed and the single distractor is correct and well grounded. Verified that head-of-bed elevation increases shear stress and that thirty-degree positioning is the recommended approach, so distractor q4_f is genuinely wrong rather than filler and its rationale is accurate. The remaining keyed interventions each map to a documented driver. THE DEFECT IS THE INVENTED DETAIL INSIDE KEYED OPTION q4_a, which directs the nurse to use 'ordered ice' and 'hearing aids'. Neither exists in this case. Asserting an ice order that the order set does not contain teaches the learner to act on a prescription that is not there, and equipping a client with hearing aids she is never documented to need or possess is a fabricated fact inside a keyed option. The substance of q4_a - premedicating twenty to thirty minutes before therapy or transfers, and using positioning and non-pharmacological supports to improve participation - is sound and should survive the repair.
contentDefects: PRIMARY: keyed option q4_a and its byChoice rationale assert 'ordered ice' and 'hearing aids', neither of which the parent establishes. The option is keyed correct, so the learner is required to select a compound action containing two fabricated elements.
bilingualVerdict: PARALLEL - stem, six options, key, rationale, six byChoice entries and strategy are semantically equivalent EN/ZH. The unestablished ice and hearing-aid elements are reproduced in ZH ('医嘱允许的冰敷' and '佩戴助听器'), so the repair is bilingual.
sourcesChecked: Pressure-injury prevention guidance located via NIH and AHRQ domain search - confirms that head-of-bed elevation increases shear stress and that thirty-degree tilt positioning is recommended, and that heels should be lifted free of the bed surface. This underwrites distractor q4_f and keyed option q4_d.
Internal search of the frozen parent for any ice order and any hearing-related finding, which returned none.
siblingImpact: NONE for the repair as scoped, which is confined to q4's option q4_a and its rationale. No stage, exhibit, title or summary text changes. If instead the alternative route is taken and an ice order plus a hearing-aid indication are authored into the baseline record, that is a global surface visible to all six parts and would require re-review of non-residual siblings q1, q2 and q6.
repairConstraints: Remove 'ordered ice' and 'hearing aids' from keyed option q4_a and its byChoice rationale in EN and ZH, retaining the premedication timing and the non-pharmacological supports that the case does establish.

Alternatively, author an ice order and a documented hearing impairment with hearing aids into the baseline record as reviewed case context - but only with re-review of the three non-residual siblings, since baseline is a global surface. The confined route is preferred.
Preserve reassessment of sedation and orthostasis before activity, which is the clinically important content of the option.
Preserve the key q4_a through q4_e and distractor q4_f unchanged in substance.
criticalNote: This is the same invented-fact pattern found in several other rows of this population, but with a material difference: here the fabrication sits inside a KEYED option rather than a distractor, so the learner is obliged to endorse it.
agreementReasoning: I searched the parent for the ice order and any hearing-related documentation before reading the proposal and found neither; Codex names the same two unsupported specifics and the same two repair routes, and proposes the same boundary I derived. I add the verified basis for distractor q4_f, which neither prior seat examined, the point that this fabrication is inside a keyed rather than a distractor option, and the sibling-exposure asymmetry that makes the confined route preferable.

reviewerDerivedProposition: A protective device has become the source of injury. The nurse removes the boot and inspects the whole heel and surrounding skin, documents size, location, colour, warmth and skin integrity and identifies the finding as a new Stage 1 device-related pressure injury, corrects the offloading so no strap crosses the calcaneus or floats the heel on a pillow under the calf, notifies through the provider or wound-care pathway and adds the heel to two-hourly skin checks, and checks the opposite heel while teaching assistive staff to verify device position at every reposition. Massaging the area and tightening the strap would intensify the exact mechanism that caused the injury.
requiredFacts: The new finding with its size, character and mechanism - stage_3: a 1.5 x 1 cm area of intact non-blanchable erythema with slight warmth on the posterior right heel where the boot strap crossed the calcaneus after shifting overnight.
The pre-existing heel-suspension boot and the left calf pillow - stage_1.
Nothing later exists; stage_3 is terminal.
disclosureEvidence: stage_3 documents the finding and its anatomical relationship to the strap but prescribes no nursing action, stages nothing, and does not use the term pressure injury. I weighed whether naming the strap as the mechanism supplies keyed options q5_b and q5_c and concluded it does not: recording where a lesion sits relative to a device is ordinary assessment documentation that a real chart would contain, and the learner must still know that intact non-blanchable erythema is Stage 1, that device-related is a distinct classification, and that offloading must eliminate rather than redistribute the strap pressure.
clinicalVerdict: Correct. Verified that a Stage 1 pressure injury is intact skin with localised non-blanchable erythema, which is exactly the finding described, and that device-associated injuries are a recognised category arising where skin is exposed to rigid medical hardware - the heel-suspension boot strap qualifies. Verified separately that massage over bony prominences and over erythematous skin is to be avoided because it generates friction and shear that damage the microcirculation, which makes distractor q5_f genuinely and importantly wrong on both of its limbs, since tightening the strap also intensifies the causative pressure. The five keyed actions form a complete and correctly sequenced response and the option set contains one real error, so discrimination is sound. I found no invented fact, no stranded value and no key ambiguity.
bilingualVerdict: PARALLEL - I read the Chinese against the English for the stem, all six options and all six byChoice rationales. Each pair is semantically equivalent, including the staging language in q5_b and the two-limbed distractor q5_f. No language-specific defect.
sourcesChecked: StatPearls pressure-injury staging (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK553107/) - read directly. Confirms 'Stage 1: Intact skin with a localized, non-blanchable area of redness (erythema)' and the recognised category of device-associated injury arising where skin is exposed to rigid medical hardware.

Pressure-injury prevention guidance located via NIH and AHRQ domain search - confirms that massage over bony prominences may be harmful and that positioning on and massaging erythematous skin should be avoided because massage causes friction and shear damaging the microcirculation. This underwrites distractor q5_f.
siblingImpact: NONE. This is an anchor-only repair; no learner-facing text changes.
repairConstraints: Set answerableAfterStageId to stage_3. No content change is required or authorised by this row.
Record explicitly in the integration ledger that this anchor is a resolver correction with no effect on the rendered page, so it is not later mistaken for a remediated leak.
criticalNote: IMPORTANT AND SPECIFIC TO THIS ROW. stage_3 is the terminal stage, so an approved stage_3 anchor hides nothing and the learner-visible surface is byte-identical before and after the repair. This is one of only two proposed anchor-only rows in the whole 66-row population whose anchor changes nothing that is rendered; I identified both structurally at the outset and examined this one on that basis. The consequence is that the audit's revealsAllStages finding here is NOMINAL: the renderer's fail-open branch happens to be showing exactly the set of stages the correct boundary would show. Setting the anchor makes the resolver agree with reality and clears the finding, which is legitimate bookkeeping, but it remediates no disclosure. The row is therefore closable ONLY because the content is sound at full visibility, which is why I examined the content rather than relying on the anchor. Had any defect been present, no anchor could have helped.
agreementReasoning: I derived stage_3 independently and agree with Codex's boundary and disposition after affirmative content review. Codex's record correctly observes that there is no later stage and that other stage_3 improvements do not determine the heel response. I add the structural point Codex does not state: because stage_3 is terminal, this anchor is a render no-op, so the row cannot be justified by the anchor at all and rests entirely on the content being sound - which I therefore verified against primary staging and prevention sources rather than accepting.
